explanation: Submitting the form starts the local UI workflow and resets the previous run. No query is started merely by editing the prompt.
The browser sends JSON containing only the prompt to its own server. The API key stays in the host process.
The server rejects requests without configuration, then validates the submitted prompt before starting a run. This excerpt is the prompt-validation boundary.
The agent function calls query once. These options belong to that single SDK invocation; the complete function closes the conversation in finally.

These actual properties configure the SDK-managed model request. tools: [] removes built-in tools, while the remaining settings disable filesystem configuration, MCP and plugins. The SDK handles transport.
This result projection reads the real model outcome and usage-related fields returned through the SDK. It is the application observation boundary, not a custom Claude API implementation.
The for-await loop consumes SDK messages and emits their explicit student-facing projection. It does not invoke a new agent for each message.
The server writes each selected event as one JSON line. Private runtime configuration and credentials are not included in this projection.
The UI updates success from the final result and shows its cost, turn count and session. Intermediate answer text alone does not mark completion.
